goal: Does empirical physical V provide different prospective guidance than entry speed error on coupled 3D turning/yawing states? No preset winner.
process_fixed: end reference at selected phase; wait .08s; normal N request/ACK; no reference resumed
physical: 3D S-shaped turn with climb/descent reversal plus 120deg yaw sweep; four entry phases

selectors.V: mean of positive residual maxima V(t)-V(t0)*exp(-.5*(t-t0)) in first100/120/160ms
selectors.simple: norm of actual velocity minus actual network target velocity at first owner-window native sample

child_operator: compress all translation knot times and switch phase by .92, divide knot velocities by .92; yaw reference remains original120deg/4s, so yaw phase also changes relative to translation. Same operator for both selectors.
shared_choice: if both choose same parent, launch one shared child and report no selection distinction
interpretation: early rollout feedback, not pre-switch certificate; matched configuration does not guarantee identical actual state; no single-factor causal claims
safety: unchanged existing protections; evidence/infrastructure failures retained; no retries
